newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes firmer in US but off fresh high vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes firmer in US but off fresh high vs yen.

text.p: The dollar ended higher after an early retreat from a fresh 42-month high against the yen was reversed by surging U.S. stocks and bonds, traders said.

The dollar's fall from early Tuesday highs against the yen was exacerbated by dollar/mark's sharp fall after forecasts that German interest rates might rise and questions over France's fiscal preparations for European Monetary Union sparked an across-the-board rush for the German currency.
But the dollar turned around in tandem with soaring U.S. asset prices after the Labor Department's employment cost index rose just 0.6 percent in the third quarter.
The wage rise was lower than Wall Street expectations and below the previous quarter's 0.8 percent increase.

"The thing is, the dollar in some respects mirrors what is going on in U.S. asset markets, and those are up sharply today," said Jim Phoenix, vice president of foreign exchange at Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, in New York.
In late trading on Tuesday, the dollar was at 1.5100/05 marks, up from 1.5090/00 at the open and 114.35/40 yen, up from 113.70/80 yen.

The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond surged almost two points as its yield fell to the lowest level in two-and-a-half months on reduced expectations that Federal Reserve policy makers will raise interest rates when they meet on November 13.
The Dow Jones stock average also jumped 34 points.

The dollar rose to 114.88 against the yen -- its highest since April 1993 -- in Tokyo on Tuesday after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in a taped interview with CNN that he was not concerned with the dollar's recent rise.

But the flight from yen was checked after Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said Japan may need to consider seriously measures regarding the foreign exchange market if it gets too volatile or failed to reflect economic fundamentals.

"What we're starting to see is a shift of comments out of Tokyo," said David Solin, partner at consulting firm Foreign Exchange Analytics. "There is obviously some discomfort with the levels here and I think what they are trying to do is just stem any sharp acceleration higher."
A final bout of profit-taking pushed the dollar to a low of 113.50 yen, before the unit reclaimed levels over 114.

The dollar tumbled against the mark in Europe after Germany's six leading economic research institutes issued a report saying that German interest rates were currently at appropriate levels but should be raised if German M3 money supply growth -- a key barometer of inflation -- remains stuck above the Bundesbank's target corridor of 4.0 to 7.0 percent.

"At the bottom of the story are interest rate differentials," said Kevin Lawrie, global foreign exchange manager at Mellon Bank. "The perception that we won't raise (interest rates) and possibly they will ... obviously it works out mark-bullish."

But the mark gave back some gains against the dollar and French franc after the European Commission denied wire service reports which said its accountants had decided to reject French plans to transfer pension funds from the state telecomunications operator to bring its budget deficit in line with requirements for Europe's single currency.
In other trade, the dollar closed at 1.2558/63 Swiss francs, up from 1.2535/45 at the open. It was off at Canadian $1.3440/45 from C$1.3456/61.
The pound rose to $1.6090/00 from $1.6055/65 at the open and the Australian dollar rose to $0.7911/16 from $0.7900/05.
